newsitem.title: USA: Son arraigned in killing of his N.Y. doctor mother.
newsitem.headline: Son arraigned in killing of his N.Y. doctor mother.

text.p: The son of a wealthy doctor, who has been charged with her murder, was arraigned Wednesday and told a New York state judge he was innocent, officials said.

James Costello, 27, was charged with second degree murder, manslaughter and criminal possession of a gun, in the shooting death of his mother, Dr. Teresita Valera-Costello, 64, a prominent gynecologist, Bronx District Attorney Robert Johnson said. She was shot twice in the head with a handgun.
Costello, who was arrested last month, was being held without bail after the assistant district attorney said he "had access to money and was a flight risk."
Costello had been the prime suspect in his mother's slaying since her body was discovered in January 1995.
Police said Costello's mother was last seen by him Dec. 3, 1994, at her luxurious Tudor-style Forest Hills Gardens home in the borough of Queens.

She was reported missing by friends a week later after she failed to show up in her native Philippines where she was to have been the keynote speaker at her alma mater, Santa Thomas University. Her plane ticket and her passport were found at her home.
Her body was found Jan. 14, 1995, stuffed in the trunk of her Mercedes-Benz, according to the indictment that was unsealed Wednesday.
Costello is alleged to have driven his mother's car to the Bronx, parked the car on a city street and walked away. Police said he never reported his mother missing.

The prosecutor said at the time of Costello's arrest that when his mother discovered her son had been stealing money from her, she confided to relatives that she was going to kick him out of her home.
He was reportedly getting a $3,000 a month allowance and allegedly feared she was going to cut him off from her $10 million estate, police sources said.
